documents.title: Medicare Annual Wellness Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Initial Medicare AWV (Medicare via ESRD since last spring).

Interval: Both Moderna doses given at the dialysis unit, 1/27 and 2/24; card reviewed and entered. Dialysis M/W/F through the right chest catheter, no line infections. Fistula surgery still not scheduled; nephrology referred to vascular, waiting list. Calving season starting, which is his busy stretch.

Health risk assessment: independent in all daily activities, drives, works the herd with one part-time hand. No falls. Hearing and vision fine for him (reading glasses). Diet: limits salt and potassium foods per the dialysis dietitian, "mostly." Wife at home, good support. PHQ-2 0. Never smoker, alcohol rare.

Exam: vitals per flowsheet. Well-appearing. Catheter site clean. Heart regular, no murmur or gallop. Lungs clear. No edema. Thigh scar unchanged.

Advance directives: wants his wife as health care proxy; form given to bring back.

Plan:
- ESRD on HD, anemia of CKD, hyperphosphatemia: per nephrology. Off-day labs today for our records.
- Cardiomyopathy: asymptomatic; due for his cardiology visit this year.
- Sarcoma history: oncology letter expected after his May scan.
- Prevention: colonoscopy 2017 (next 2027). Flu done in the fall. COVID primary series complete. Shingrix in the fall. Pneumococcal vaccine to discuss next year.
- Written prevention schedule given.

documents.title: Sarcoma Surveillance Visit (outside oncology)
documents.author: oncology
documents.body:
Sarcoma survivorship clinic, visit of 2021-05-18.

Mr. Upton returns for routine surveillance seven years after wide local excision of a soft-tissue sarcoma of the right thigh followed by doxorubicin-based chemotherapy (2014). He has no new lumps, thigh pain or cough. Weight steady. He is now on hemodialysis, which began in April 2020.

Exam: right thigh scar well healed, no palpable mass or induration along the excision bed, inguinal nodes not enlarged. Lungs clear.

CT chest today: no pulmonary nodules or other evidence of metastatic disease.

Impression: no evidence of recurrence. Continue annual surveillance with exam and chest imaging through year 10. He continues to see cardiology for his anthracycline-related LV dysfunction.

Allergies: NKDA. Medications per his list.

Thank you for letting us share in his care.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Primary Care Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Routine. Haying done for the first cut, second cut coming. Dialysis going steadily, no missed runs. Saw cardiology in July; told "no change" and keep the same pills (no letter received). Oncology letter in May clean. Health care proxy form returned, scanned.

O: Vitals per flowsheet. Tanned, well. Catheter site clean. Heart regular. Lungs clear. No edema.

A/P: ESRD on HD, anemia of CKD, phos per nephrology. Cardiomyopathy stable, asymptomatic. Will request the cardiology note. Flu in October; Shingrix after that. RTC 6 months for AWV.

documents.title: Nurse Visit — Influenza
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Flu vaccine 0.5 mL IM right deltoid. Screening negative. Patient reports Moderna booster at his dialysis unit on 10/4; entered from his card. Shingrix #1 scheduled 11/16 so the two aren't on the same day per his preference.

documents.title: Nurse Visit — Shingrix #1
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Shingrix 0.5 mL IM right deltoid, dose 1 of 2. Told him to expect a sore arm and maybe a day of feeling run down, and to schedule it for after a dialysis day if he can. Dose 2 due in 2 to 6 months; will give at his March AWV.

documents.title: Medicare Annual Wellness Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Subsequent AWV.

Interval: no ED visits or hospital stays. Dialysis three days a week, still by the chest catheter. Nephrology has him on the vascular surgery list again; he says the first referral "got lost." Cardiology visit last summer reportedly unchanged; note never arrived despite our request.

HRA: independent, working full days on non-dialysis days. No falls. Mood good, PHQ-2 0. Sleeps well. Safety: wears a seat belt. Proxy on file (wife).

Exam: vitals per flowsheet. Well. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft. No edema.

Plan:
- Shingrix #2 and PCV20 today (CKD and heart disease both qualify him).
- Labs for our records.
- ESRD, anemia, phos per nephrology; cardiomyopathy asymptomatic, continue lisinopril and furosemide.
- Colonoscopy due 2027.
RTC 6 months.

documents.title: Pharmacy refill request: furosemide, lisinopril
documents.author: MA
documents.body:
Electronic refill requests from his pharmacy for furosemide 40 mg daily and lisinopril 10 mg daily, 90-day supply each. Last office visit 3/8/22. Routed to PCP.

PCP: Approved both, 90 days with 3 refills. Binders and epoetin stay with nephrology.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Primary Care Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Six-month check. Finally saw vascular surgery in July after the nephrology re-referral; left forearm fistula planned for early October. He's glad to be rid of the catheter eventually. No problems with it so far. Otherwise feels well, working. No breathlessness, no swelling.

O: Vitals per flowsheet. Well. Catheter right chest, site clean. Heart regular. Lungs clear. No edema.

A/P:
- ESRD on HD, access planning under way. He asked about aspirin before surgery; told him to follow the surgeon's instructions.
- Cardiomyopathy asymptomatic.
- Flu and updated COVID shot this fall at the dialysis unit or here, his choice.
RTC after surgery.

documents.title: Surgery Friday
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi, this is Adam's wife writing for him. His fistula surgery is this Friday the 7th. The surgeon's office said he can keep taking his baby aspirin. Do you need anything from us beforehand? Thanks.

documents.title: RE: Surgery Friday
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Thanks for letting us know. Nothing needed from our side, the surgeon's instructions are the ones to follow. Please have him book a visit with us a few weeks after surgery. Good luck Friday.

documents.title: Vascular Surgery Post-operative Visit
documents.author: vascular surgery
documents.body:
Vascular surgery clinic, date of service 2022-10-21. Faxed to PCP.

55-year-old man on in-center hemodialysis by tunneled catheter, seen two weeks after creation of a left forearm arteriovenous fistula (10/7/22).

He has felt more tired since surgery and gets mildly short of breath going up stairs, which he thinks is his anemia. Denies chest pain, leg swelling or needing to sleep propped up. Incision pain minimal.

Vitals: T 98.7 F (37.1 C), HR 104, BP 132/64, RR 16, SpO2 98% on room air.

Exam: incision healing well, no drainage. Hand warm, extremities warm with bounding peripheral pulses. Prominent bruit over the fistula with a palpable continuous thrill. Apical impulse displaced laterally.

Assessment: healing left forearm AV fistula, maturing as expected.
Plan: dialysis unit may begin cannulation trials once maturity is confirmed, typically 4 to 6 weeks; keep the tunneled catheter until the fistula is reliably in use. Arm exercises reviewed. His fatigue and exertional breathlessness to be followed by nephrology and his primary care physician.

Allergies: NKDA. Meds: calcium acetate, sevelamer, epoetin alfa, lisinopril, furosemide, aspirin 81, multivitamin, acetaminophen as needed.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Primary Care Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Four weeks out from the left forearm fistula. Vascular surgery note received. Since surgery he's been more tired and a little winded on the stairs to the hayloft. Thinks it's his blood count. No chest pain, no swelling, sleeps flat on one pillow. Dialysis still by catheter while the fistula matures. Flu shot 9/28 and bivalent COVID 10/12 at the dialysis unit.

O: Vitals per flowsheet. Comfortable. Left forearm incision healed; thrill and bruit over the fistula. Catheter site clean. JVP not elevated. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. No edema.

A/P:
- Fatigue and mild exertional dyspnea since fistula creation. CBC and BMP today. Will send results and this note to nephrology, who see him three times a week and can adjust from there.
- ESRD on HD, new AV fistula maturing.
- Cardiomyopathy: no signs of fluid today.
RTC 3 to 4 months, sooner if worse.
